newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-S&P rates Australia's Eastern Energy A minus.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-S&P rates Australia's Eastern Energy A minus.

text.p: Ratings agency Standard & Poors Corp said on Monday it had assigned its A-minus long term and A-2 short term local and foreign currency credit ratings to Australian power utility Eastern Energy Ltd.
It said the rating outlook was stable.

"The ratings reflect the stable regulatory regime under which Eastern Energy operates, the diversity of its customer base and service area, and the insulation from competitive pressure in Eastern Energy's franchise network business," S&P said.
"These factors are offset somewhat by its modest financial profile," it said.
Texas Utilities Electric Co bought Eastern Energy from the Victorian government in November last year for A$2.127 billion.

S&P said Eastern Energy was able to sustain a higher rating than its U.S. parent, which was rated at BBB+/A-2, because they operated under different legal and regulatory regimes and there was an expectation Texas Utilities would sell down its stake.
"Eastern Energy's stable business environment stems from network business' transparent regulatory regime and predictable revenue stream, which provides the majority of earnings," S&P said.

It said Eastern Energy's financial profile was characterised by low interest coverage levels, with funds-flow to interest coverage currently below two times, but was expected to reach three times by about the year 2000.
"The debt payback period is currently around 15 years, but is forecast to reduce to below 10 years in the medium term as cash flow generated from operations is used to retire debt," S&P said.
